newsitem.title: USA: Autotote to sell unit to Scientific Games.
newsitem.headline: Autotote to sell unit to Scientific Games.

text.p: Gambling equipment company Autotote Corp. has agreed to sell its European lottery business, Tele Control, to Scientific Games Holdings Corp. for $25 million to $29.5 million, the companies said Tuesday.
Tele Control, an online lottery and transaction processing company, generated fiscal 1996 revenues of about $27 million, Scientific Games said.

"The sale of Tele Control continues our concentration on our core businesses and also strengthens our company by allowing us to significantly reduce our bank debt," said Lorne Weil, Autotote chairman.
"At the same time, however, the sale will affect neither our domestic lottery activity, nor our other international lottery customers not served by Tele Control."
The deal is subject to a definitive agreement and certain third party consents, the companies said.
The exact purchase price will be determined by a formula reflecting changes in the net assets of Tele Control from Oct. 31, Scientific Games said.
Atlanta-based Scientific Games is a leading worldwide manufacturer of instant lottery tickets and provider of lottery support services.

Autotote, based in New York, provides gambling, equipment, computer software, facilities management and satellite broadcast services for on-track, off-track and inter-track wagering, lotteries, and legalised sports betting facilities.
Autotote's stock rose 12.5 cents to $1.75 early on the American Stock Exchange. Scientific Games rose 25 cents to $26.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
